n50eda6cd34b.s: Which of the following was true of Vijayanagara provincial governors?
o: They could not keep their own armies
They held office for life without transfer
n50eda6cd34b.x: Governors could mint coins, levy taxes and keep armies, but they were frequently transferred.

n8085e5d9db2.s: What was the chief export of the Vijayanagara empire?
n8085e5d9db2.x: Kalamkari was the chief export; horses were the chief import and Chinese silk was also imported.

n87ee9763db1.s: Which traveller described Vijayanagara as a city 'the eye had not seen'?
n87ee9763db1.x: Abdur Razzaq recorded this, along with the prostitution tax paid to the guards and the absence of purdah.

n9c1287b81f2.s: Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti were Vijayanagara centres of:
n9c1287b81f2.x: Tadipatri, Adoni and Gutti were textile centres; Vajrakarur was known for diamonds.

new.s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva dynasty?
new.x: Vira Narasimha founded the Tuluva dynasty in 1505. His father Tuluva Narasa Nayaka helped both usurpations but was not the founder.

new.s: In 1505, Vira Narasimha killed Immadi Narasimha, the last Saluva ruler, at:
new.x: The second usurpation took place at Penugonda, where Vira Narasimha killed Immadi Narasimha and began the Tuluva dynasty.

new.s: In the first usurpation of 1485, Saluva Narasimha expelled:
new.x: Saluva Narasimha of Chandragiri expelled Praudha Raya in 1485, ending the Sangama dynasty.

new.s: In which year did the second usurpation, which began the Tuluva dynasty, take place?
new.x: The second usurpation was in 1505; the first (Saluva) was in 1485.

new.s: Krishnadevaraya was crowned on 8 August of which year?
new.x: The Hampi inscription dates his coronation to 8 August 1509.

new.s: Saluvabhyudayam, the work on Saluva Narasimha, was written by:
new.x: Rajanatha Dindima was Saluva Narasimha's court poet and wrote Saluvabhyudayam.

new.s: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to which Gajapati ruler?
new.x: Saluva Narasimha lost Udayagiri to Gajapati Purushottama; Krishnadevaraya later won it back from Prataparudra.

new.s: Saluva Narasimha moved his capital from Kalyanapuram to:
new.x: Saluva Narasimha's capital shifted from Kalyanapuram to Chandragiri.

new.s: Krishnadevaraya took Gulbarga in:
new.x: After routing Ismail Adil Shah at Raichur in 1520, he took Gulbarga in 1523.

new.s: Krishnadevaraya earned the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya by freeing which Sultan from Ali Barid?
new.x: In the Raichur-Bidar campaign of 1510 he restored the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah, freeing him from Ali Barid.

new.s: After taking Kondaveedu, Krishnadevaraya performed the Talapurusha Danam at:
new.x: Kondaveedu was taken with Saluva Timmarusu's help, after which the king performed Talapurusha Danam at Amaravati.

new.s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign reach Cuttack?
new.x: Cuttack was reached in 1518 and the Gajapati sued for peace.

new.s: Under the peace with Prataparudra Gajapati, which lands went back to the Gajapati?
new.x: Prataparudra gave his daughter in marriage, and the lands north of the Krishna were returned to him.

new.s: At which temple did Krishnadevaraya present a diamond necklace to Varaha Narasimha?
new.x: He gave a diamond necklace at Simhachalam; at Mangalagiri he gave land to Lakshmi Narasimha.

new.s: The town Nagalapuram founded by Krishnadevaraya was named after his:
new.x: Nagalapuram was named after his mother Nagalamba; Hospet after Queen Tirumaladevi.

new.s: Hospet, also called Tirumaladevipattana, was named after:
new.x: Krishnadevaraya named Hospet after his queen Tirumaladevi.

new.s: The title 'Gajabetekara' belonged to:
new.x: Gajabetekara is Devaraya II's title and is a common decoy among Krishnadevaraya's titles.

new.s: According to legend, which deity told Krishnadevaraya in a dream to write Amuktamalyada?
new.x: The legend says Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam (Krishna district) appeared in a dream during the Kalinga campaign.

new.s: Amuktamalyada narrates the marriage of Goda Devi (Andal) with:
new.x: Its theme is Goda Devi (Andal) and her marriage to Sri Ranganatha; the work is dedicated to Venkateswara.

new.s: Amuktamalyada is also known as:
new.x: Amuktamalyada is also called Vishnuchittiyam; the other three are works of the Ashtadiggajas.

new.s: Which of the following works of Krishnadevaraya is NOT in Sanskrit?
new.x: Amuktamalyada is his only Telugu work; Madalasa Charita, Rasamanjari and Usha Parinayam are in Sanskrit.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Amuktamalyada:
1. It records the genealogy of the dynasty from Bukka to Krishnadevaraya.
2. It describes the invasions of Krishnadevaraya.
3. It discusses statecraft (rajaniti) and kingship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Amuktamalyada does not describe his invasions (APPSC G2 2003).

new.s: Varadambika Parinayam, on the marriage of Achyutaraya, was written by:
new.x: Tirumalamba of Achyutaraya's court wrote Varadambika Parinayam, a Sanskrit champu.

new.s: Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam describes:
o: The marriage of Achyutaraya and Varadambika
new.x: Gangadevi, queen of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam on Kampana's conquest of Madurai.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (poet – work) is correctly matched?
new.x: Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam; Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.

new.s: Tirumalamba's Varadambika Parinayam is a Sanskrit:
new.x: Varadambika Parinayam is a Sanskrit champu.

new.s: Parijatapaharanamu was written by which Ashtadiggaja?
new.x: Nandi Timmana, known as Mukku Timmana, wrote Parijatapaharanamu.

new.s: The title 'Prabandha Parameshwara' belongs to:
new.x: Prabandha Parameshwara is Errana's title, not Nandi Timmana's.

new.s: Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam was written by the Shaiva poet:
new.x: Dhurjati, the Shaiva poet of Kalahasti, wrote Sri Kalahasteeswara Mahatyam and Satakam.

new.s: Vasucharitramu, dedicated to Tirumala Raya, was written by:
new.x: Ramarajabhushana (Bhattumurti) wrote Vasucharitramu and Narasabhupaliyamu.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (poet – work) is correctly matched?
new.x: Madayyagari Mallana wrote Rajasekhara Charitramu; Ramabhyudayamu is Ramabhadrudu's, Panduranga Mahatmyamu Tenali Ramakrishna's and Vasucharitramu Ramarajabhushana's.

new.s: The term 'Bhuvana Vijayam' literally means:
new.x: Bhuvana Vijayam means 'conquest of the world'; Ashtadiggajas means eight elephants and Kavula Samstha institution of poets.

new.s: Fernao Nuniz, who wrote on Krishnadevaraya's rise, visited Vijayanagara during the reign of:
new.x: Nuniz wrote on Krishnadevaraya but visited under Achyutaraya; Paes described Krishnadevaraya's court.

new.s: Aliya Rama Raya belonged to which family?
new.x: Aliya Rama Raya, Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law, was of the Aravidu family.

new.s: Aliya Rama Raya killed which rival in 1543 before making Sadasiva a figurehead?
new.x: Rama Raya killed Salakam Tirumala in 1543 and made Sadasiva a figurehead.

new.s: Which historian described the Vijayanagara state as a 'military administration'?
new.x: Nilakanta Sastri called it a military administration; Burton Stein called it a segmentary state.

new.s: In Vijayanagara administration, the Athavane department dealt with:
new.x: Athavane was the revenue department; Kandachara was military and Bhandara the treasury.

new.s: The Bhandara (Sri Bhandara) department of Vijayanagara was the:
new.x: Bhandara was the treasury; Athavane handled revenue.

new.s: According to the Rayavachakam, how many departments were there in the Vijayanagara administration?
new.x: The Rayavachakam records nine departments, each headed by a Samprati.

new.s: The chief minister heading the pradhanis in Vijayanagara was called the:
new.x: The Mahapradhani headed the pradhanis (e.g. Saluva Timmarusu); the Dalavayi was commander-in-chief.

new.s: According to Amuktamalyada, the bulk of the king's revenue should go to the:
new.x: Amuktamalyada advises that the bulk of revenue go to the army.

new.s: Amuktamalyada advises that forts should be commanded by:
new.x: Krishnadevaraya's maxim was that Brahmins should command forts.

new.s: The Sangama princes who governed Vijayanagara provinces held the title:
new.x: Princes governing a Rajya or Mandala under the Sangamas were titled Odeyar.

new.s: Before 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of which Andhra rajya?
new.x: Saluva Narasimha governed Chandragiri before 1485; it later became a capital.

new.s: Which Andhra rajya became the new headquarters of Tirumala after Talikota?
new.x: After Talikota, Penukonda became Tirumala's new headquarters.

new.s: About how many rajyams were there under Achyutaraya?
new.x: There were about 17 rajyams under Achyutaraya.

new.s: The tribute paid by the Vijayanagara amaranayakas to the king was called:
new.x: Amaranayakas paid tribute called Kappam and kept troops, horses and elephants for the king.

new.s: About how many nayakas held amarams under the Vijayanagara amara-nayankara system?
new.x: Vijayanagara had about 200 nayakas, against the Kakatiyas' 75 or 77.

new.s: The Kakatiya nayankara system had how many nayakas?
new.x: The Kakatiya system had 75 or 77 nayakas holding mandalams and forts; Vijayanagara had about 200.

new.s: Which independent Nayaka states arose out of the amara-nayankara system after 1565?
new.x: After 1565 the nayakas formed independent states at Madurai, Tanjore and Keladi.

new.s: In Vijayanagara villages, 'Merulu' were the grain gifts collected by the:
new.x: The Talari (watchman) collected Merulu; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share.

new.s: Which village officer kept the accounts and land and crop registers in Vijayanagara villages?
new.x: The Karanam kept accounts, land and crop registers and temple accounts; the Reddi was the village head.

new.s: In a Vijayanagara village, forced labour (vetti) was supervised by the:
new.x: The Begari supervised vetti (forced labour).

new.s: In Vijayanagara revenue terms, Navidadere was a tax on:
new.x: Navidadere (Kondaju) was the barbers' tax; Maneyanna was the house tax.

new.s: Maneyanna (Illari Pannu) in Vijayanagara was a tax on:
new.x: Maneyanna was the house tax.

new.s: Who abolished the marriage tax in the Vijayanagara empire?
new.x: Saluva Narasimha first remitted the marriage tax; Krishnadevaraya abolished it.

new.s: The usual share of produce collected as land revenue in Vijayanagara was:
new.x: The usual share was 1/6; fertile land paid 1/4 or 1/3.

new.s: Which Vijayanagara tax was levied on the birth of a son?
new.x: Putrodaya Kanuka was levied on the birth of a son; Kalyana Kanika was the wedding tax.

new.s: The Siddha (standing) army of Vijayanagara was paid every:
new.x: The standing army was paid every four months.

new.s: In the Vijayanagara period, forts were placed under the:
new.x: The four kinds of forts were under Durga Dannayakas.

new.s: In the Vijayanagara period, a Brahmin guilty of a crime punishable by death received:
new.x: Brahmins got life imprisonment instead of death.

new.s: Under the Kavali system, policing at the Sthala level was done by the:
new.x: Talari policed the village, Kavali Daru the sthala and Peta Kavalidaru the towns.

new.s: Under the Vijayanagara Kavali system, towns were policed by the:
new.x: Towns were policed by the Peta Kavalidaru.

new.s: Who was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara?
new.x: Ibn Battuta of Morocco came under Harihara I; Nicolo Conti was the earliest European visitor.

new.s: Athanasius Nikitin, author of 'Journey Beyond Three Seas', came from:
new.x: Nikitin was Russian and visited the Bahmani kingdom; Abdur Razzaq was Persian.

new.s: Caesar Frederick, who saw the ruined capital after Talikota, visited Vijayanagara in:
new.x: Caesar Frederick of Venice came in 1567, under Sadasiva.

new.s: The accounts of Paes and Nuniz were translated by Robert Sewell in:
new.x: Robert Sewell translated them in A Forgotten Empire (1900).

new.s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara as the envoy of:
new.x: Abdur Razzaq was the Timurid envoy of Shah Rukh and came in 1443.

new.s: Nicolo de Conti estimated the Vijayanagara army at:
new.x: Conti put the army at 90,000 and the city at 60 miles round; Nuniz gave 600,000 amara troops.

new.s: In Vijayanagara society, the Vira Panchalas were:
new.x: The Vira Panchalas worked in gold, iron, brass, wood and stone.

new.s: In Vijayanagara society, the Niyogis were:
new.x: Niyogis were Brahmin officials; Vaidikas were priests.

new.s: The Idangai (left-hand) division of Vijayanagara society consisted mainly of:
new.x: Idangai were mainly artisans (including Panchala smiths); Valangai were agricultural and trading groups.

new.s: In Vijayanagara society, 'Kanyashulkam' meant:
new.x: Kanyashulkam was bride price; Varashulkam was dowry.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women in Vijayanagara society?
o: Women served as bodyguards and wrestlers
new.x: There was no strict purdah; the other three statements are correct.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Christian missions under Vijayanagara:
1. Venkatapati Raya II allowed a church at Chandragiri.
2. Venkatapati Raya II belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Venkatapati Raya II allowed the Chandragiri church and protected the Jesuit mission, but he was an Aravidu ruler.

new.s: The guru of the Sangama rulers was:
new.x: The Shaiva Sangamas had Kalamukha Kriya Shakti as guru and Virupaksha as family deity.

new.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler enlisted Muslims in the army and built a mosque?
new.x: Devaraya II enlisted Muslims in the army with jagirs and built a mosque.

new.s: Under which ruler did Tirupati rise to prominence?
new.x: Tirupati rose under Saluva Narasimha, as the later dynasties were Vaishnava.

new.s: With which festival did the Vijayanagara financial year begin?
new.x: The financial year began with Mahanavami, when the nayakas brought tribute.

new.s: Which traveller recorded that 250 buffaloes and 400 goats were sacrificed on the last day of Mahanavami?
new.x: Domingo Paes recorded the Mahanavami sacrifices.

new.s: Kuchipudi dance was founded by:
new.x: Kuchipudi grew from the Bhagavata Mela and was founded by Siddhendra Yogi.

new.s: The earlier form of Yakshagana was:
new.x: Koravanji was the earlier form of Yakshagana.

new.s: Burrakatha developed from which tradition?
new.x: Burrakatha is a Telugu storytelling form from the Jangam Katha tradition.

new.s: The Porumamilla inscription was issued by:
new.x: Bhaskara Mantri issued it in 1369, in Bukka I's time, recording the Anantasagaram tank.

new.s: The Siruveru tank near Penukonda was built by:
new.x: Bukka I built the Siruveru tank; Saluva Narasimha built Narasambudhi.

new.s: The main source of revenue in the Vijayanagara economy was:
new.x: Land tax was the main revenue source.

new.s: Which of the following was a west-coast port of the Vijayanagara period?
new.x: Bhatkal was on the west coast; Pulicat, Motupalli and Machilipatnam were east-coast ports.

new.s: In the Vijayanagara period, Venkatagiri was known for:
new.x: Venkatagiri was known for zari; Gutti and Rayadurg for silk.

new.s: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416) is linked with which ruler, who took Motupalli?
new.x: Devaraya I took Motupalli; the Motupalli Dharma Sasanam dates to 1416.

new.s: The Pratapa (Mada) coin of Vijayanagara was worth:
new.x: The gold Pratapa was half a varaha; the panam was one-tenth of a pratapa.

new.s: The Tar coin of Vijayanagara was made of:
new.x: Tar and Pesado were silver; Jital and Kasu were copper.

new.s: Which Vijayanagara coins were made of copper?
new.x: Jital and Kasu were copper coins.
